$comment: Scripts that CANNOT run in CI, each with the reason. Read by tools/check-script-coverage.mjs.
This file is not a place to hide a script: every entry needs a reason of 20+ characters, and
an entry becomes a FAILURE the moment the script is referenced again or deleted. The three
reasons below are the only three shapes that exist here: needs a local DSH installation,
inspects a local profile, or is a one-off authored during an audit.

scripts.verify-params.mjs: Needs a local DSH installation: it compiles the tool definitions through the real @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools from the vendored asar, which a CI runner does not have. The static parameter-shaped checks are covered by verify-manifest.mjs in CI.
scripts.verify-bundle.mjs: Needs a local DSH installation: it imports index.js and the tool registry, which resolve @deepseek-ai/* packages reconstructed from the local asar. Its static half is verify-manifest.mjs, which DOES run in CI.
scripts.check-profile.mjs: Inspects the installed Harness profile on this machine (its package.json and node_modules); a CI runner has no profile to inspect, so the check would report UNVERIFIED on every run.
scripts.check-report.mjs: Reads the recurrence report produced by earlier local verification runs; there is no such report on a fresh CI checkout, so it can only be run after those runs exist.
scripts.asar-list.mjs: One-off reconnaissance used during the audit to list entries inside a DSH app.asar; kept so the measurement can be reproduced, not part of any delivery gate.
scripts.repo-recon.mjs: One-off reconnaissance used during the audit to dump a reference repository's structure; kept so the comparison can be reproduced, not part of any delivery gate.
